owned: agent/laptop.py say and cap-specific execution budget only
scope.coordination: Parent owns beat imports/capabilities/session cleanup in shared laptop.py; core_access_integration owns native helper receipts and timeout glue.

trigger.source: Root-reported live native multitool observation; not independently replayed by this worker.
trigger.observed: Explicit device say acknowledged, followed by automatic final narration returning UNKNOWN at the existing four-second deadline.
trigger.inference: Avoid duplicate attempted speech and align the server, bridge and driver deadlines, rather than narrowing ordinary answers to fit a four-second OS cap.

decision.duplicate_speech: Immutable CompletedReply optional trailing explicit_speech_attempted=False; true consumes the native thread/turn once and records EXPLICIT_SPEECH_ATTEMPTED before any automatic Bus call.
decision.receipt_source_contract: Native device helper sets the flag at actual Bus dispatch for say. Includes later UNKNOWN/cancellation; excludes pre-send refusal. Integration owner implements and tests that glue separately.
decision.presentation: Whole safe first line within the driver-supported 160 characters; otherwise a safe first sentence within that limit, or the fixed chat fallback. No word-count or pronunciation cap. Whole greeting and ordinary eleven-/thirteen-word replies remain intact.
decision.auto_deadline: ConversationSpeech default 15 seconds, configured from native conversation cleanup timeout by integration owner; min configured budget/live lease remaining. Exact authority is rechecked by existing Bus callback after queueing.
decision.driver_deadline: Only say receives the full remaining authenticated frame deadline. Other existing OS commands retain their four-second bound. Rendering is bounded, actual AIFF duration is read using Python 3.12 aifc, and playback is refused before launch unless clip duration plus one-second player allowance and 250ms acknowledgment margin fits remaining time.
decision.uncertainty: A failed/timeout file render reports FAILED with no playback; malformed/missing/zero-length duration is refused. Once afplay starts, timeout remains UNKNOWN and is never retried. Driver returns nominal rendered_duration_ms, not acoustic latency or audibility.
decision.unchanged: Full text remains in guest chat. No web edits, model service, automatic replay, output-device changes or volume changes.

verification.fixtures: Synthetic silent AIFF metadata/data and injected subprocess runner only; no subprocess, speech engine, playback or model calls.
cases: True explicit-speech receipt skips automatic output once without parsing final prose.
True uncertain-speech receipt never queues behind the speaker lock or substitutes/replays after another speaker appears.
Receipt flag stays immutable and absent from wire JSON; older six-argument constructors keep the false default.
Mentioning speech in prose is not an authoritative dispatch receipt.
Whole greeting and meaningful eleven-/thirteen-word sentences remain intact; long/code/link/private-marker prose still uses the safe fallback.
A five-second synthetic rendered clip is allowed with a fifteen-second deadline and gets a six-second bounded player budget.
A clip that cannot fit actual remaining budget, expired rendering, missing/malformed/zero-duration audio never starts a player.
Speech gets the real remaining frame deadline instead of four seconds; other controls retain four seconds; expired executor work never dispatches.
Automatic speech frame deadline cannot outlast its current lease.
Existing post-text order, reconnect/cancellation, revoked/expired queued speech, UNKNOWN and transport-failure checks still pass.

limits: One-second player and 250ms acknowledgment allowances are conservative engineering margins, not measured guarantees; real Mac validation remains required.
Actual rendered AIFF duration is nominal file duration, not optical/acoustic onset or end-to-end physical latency.
Root must deploy and verify ordinary greeting plus explicit tool speech without duplicate final narration using the actual audio bridge.
Broad OS speech invoked outside the native device helper is not intercepted by this receipt flag.
Already-started physical playback cannot be undone by ordinary revocation; UNKNOWN is never replayed.
